theme: Weekly Patterns Vol.2 — Tier 2 stats (HOD/LOD timing, range vs monthly, wick patterns, sequential closes)

stat_6_hod_lod_by_dow.description: For each weekly session, which day of the week made the high (HOD) and the low (LOD)? Run on NQ1! daily Globex chart. Note: NQ futures Globex daily bars open at 6 PM ET the prior calendar day, so Pine's `dayofweek` is offset relative to RTH session day. Below shows both the Pine label AND the corresponding RTH trading day.
stat_6_hod_lod_by_dow.convention_note: Pine dayofweek=1 (Sunday eve open) = Monday RTH trading day. dayofweek=5 (Thursday eve open) = Friday RTH trading day. We never see dayofweek=6/7 because Friday eve / Saturday have no Globex session.
stat_6_hod_lod_by_dow.key_finding: Friday makes the weekly HIGH 34% of the time (highest of any day). Monday makes the weekly LOW 33% of the time (highest of any day). Together, Mon-Fri is asymmetric: highs lean toward end-of-week, lows toward start-of-week. The 'sell Monday, buy Friday' framing is statistically supported by 1,400 weeks of data.

stat_7_week_pct_of_4week_range.description: Each week's range expressed as % of the trailing 4-week range (used as monthly-equivalent). Bucketed distribution.
stat_7_week_pct_of_4week_range.interpretation: Average week makes ~52% of its 4-week range. About half of weeks (47.56%) make 25-50% of the 4-week range. About 14% of weeks alone establish 75%+ of the 4-week range — these are the dominant weeks that 'set the month.'

stat_8_wick_week_patterns.description: Reversal patterns based on weekly candle structure.

rows.pattern: Shooting star (long upper wick + red close)

stat_8_wick_week_patterns.key_finding: Hammer (long-lower-wick + green close) is the cleanest weekly wick pattern at 60.5% green-next (n=119). Shooting stars (mirror pattern) are essentially worthless on NQ weekly — only 51.61% red-next. Asymmetry consistent with NQ's upward drift bias.

stat_9_sequential_higher_closes.description: Strict sequential progression of weekly closes — each close higher than the prior. Stricter than streak-by-color (which only requires same-color, not monotonic).

after_n_lower_closes_p_higher_next.verdict: Counter-intuitive — same anomaly as Vol.1 streak stat. 3 sequential lower closes does NOT bounce.

stat_9_sequential_higher_closes.key_finding: The 3-sequential-lower-closes anomaly mirrors the 3-red-streak anomaly from Vol.1 (42.03% vs 41.94% — almost identical). This confirms the pattern: the 3rd consecutive down week does NOT bounce. By the 4th down week it snaps back at 66.67%. Same pattern measured two ways with the same result is strong evidence.
